messages.subject: documentation on ggplot_gtable and ggplot_build
parts:
Someone asked this question, which tops google search with either
'ggplot_gtable' or 'ggplot_build' as keyword:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/16268532/r-documentation-on-ggplot-gtable-and-ggplot-build

I found in general ggplot2 is rather laconic in the man pages, while 'R
cookbook' is much richer in detail. This is the opposite of the intention of
these documents: a cookbook should be like a teacher, more instructive than
informative, while a manual should be like a dictionary, to cover all
points.

Anyway, perhaps it could start from naï¿œve questions of a newbie like me to
show the public (googlers) the pieces of the jigsaw.

Issue to document, No.1: Can the return value of ggplot_build serve any
other purpose than being used, modified or not, as parameter of
ggplot_gtable? If so, this should be documented.

After some experiments I found the return value of ggplot_build is
printable. printing it results a half-pageful of console output and
a new graph being plotted on the default output device. So the
answer is: ggplot_build can be used without ggplot_gtable.

But then again, profiling shows that there is no speed advantage of
printing the orignal graph, comparing with printing the return value
of ggplot_build(original_graph); so the new answer is:
performance-wise, there is no reason to print the return value than
to use it as parameter of ggplot_gtable.

# my experiment data
> p <- ggplot(data, aes(x=timestamp, y=profit,fill=profit_threshold)) + geom_line()

# printing the graph directly
> system.time(print(p)) # a graph is plotted on default output dev.
user system elapsed
29.222 0.316 29.704
Warning message:
Removed 9074 rows containing missing values (geom_path).

# ggplot_build took almost the same amount of time, so some work
# must have been done in it.
> system.time(q<-ggplot_build(p))
user system elapsed 25.430 0.160 25.661 Warning message:
Removed 9074 rows containing missing values (geom_path).

# surprisingly, printing the return value of ggplot_build again
# take the same amount of time as printing original p -- so what
# work was done in ggplot_build??
> system.time(print(p)) # a graph is plotted on default output dev.
user system elapsed 27.506 0.232 27.928 Warning message:
Removed 9074 rows containing missing values (geom_path).

Issue to document, No.2: ggplot_build must intend to offer an opportunity to
alter the chart before plotted - otherwise, a single function
ggplot_gtable_build() would suffice - then how could the alteration be done?
That requires documenting the data structure of return value of
ggplot_build().
